stage1.impression: A warm, moody bar shot that reads at first glance like a hotel bar in a timber library, not a specific listening bar: the brightest thing in the frame is an empty grid of lit pigeonholes, and the two speakers in their niches read as washed-out grey-white boxes behind a sepia veil, not as the hero. At 1:1 the timber is smooth and evenly coloured, the whole frame has an orange monochrome grade, the haze shafts look staged, and the identical stool copies and the crushed black chair back in the foreground say CG. A magazine would see a generic, competent render, not a specific place.

blocking_9: The record wall must be full of records (spines, a few faced-out sleeves) and darker than the speakers; right now it is empty cubbies and the brightest large area (median 132 vs speaker 69)
The speakers must be the first read: smoked acrylic tint and horn visible against a darker niche, not a grey-white box against a white-lit niche back (right niche median 171, clip 1.4 %)
The grade must let neutrals be neutral: concrete and zinc grey-warm, not everything in one orange-brown (ceiling R/G/B medians 61/30/11)
Visible shell materials with texture at 1:1: board-formed concrete, checked fir beams, blackened steel; at present timber everywhere, smooth and untextured
No crushed foreground mass: the chair back at 270-540 x 610-800 is a black hole (median 4.5)
Haze reads as atmosphere, not as stage beams

defects.what: Record wall cubbies are empty and evenly lit; brightest large area of the frame, reads as an unstocked showroom shelf
Left speaker reads as a grey/white box with the white batts dominating; no smoked tint read; niche back above the horn lit near white
Right speaker washed out by the lit niche strip, median 171, clip 1.43 %; reads as a white box
Ceiling and beams strongly orange (R61 G30 B11), smooth, no checks or end grain
Hard diagonal haze shaft from a ceiling spot reads as a stage beam
Foreground chair back crushed to black (median 4.5, crush 11 %), a dead mass in the lower left third
Identical stool and chair models repeated in a row
Dome pendant liner reads milky white, its smoked tint lost; nearly clipped (median 218)
Record players and glassware at the decks read as a flat grey glass box; no clean reflections or glowing edges
Whole-frame sepia grade; no neutral surfaces; little concrete or steel visible, so the place reads as generic timber bar

changes.problem: The record wall is empty and is the brightest large area, so it steals the frame from the speakers and makes the room look unfinished.

evidence.measured: lum_median 131.8, p95 219.6; cubbies visibly empty in a 2x crop, only one cubby holds a few sleeves

change.setting: props: records on the record wall
change.to: every cubby filled with records spine-out, about 85 % full, with 3 to 4 sleeves faced out and one cubby half empty with a leaning stack

changes.expected: The wall becomes a dark, textured mass of spines with small highlights; its median falls by about half and the frame reads as a listening bar.

changes.problem: The lit niche strip washes the speakers and the niche backs to near white, so the smoked acrylic does not read and the speakers look like grey boxes.

evidence.measured: lum_median 170.7, clip 1.43 %; left niche p95 218 with the white niche back above the horn

changes.expected: Niche backs drop to a warm mid-tone; the speakers' smoked tint and horn edges read against them; clipping in the niche goes away.

changes.problem: The record wall spots add a second bright wash that competes with the speakers.

change.setting: lamps: the record wall 4 x spot

changes.expected: Pools on the spines instead of an even glow; the speakers become the brightest designed objects after the lamps.

changes.problem: The grade turns everything orange-brown, so concrete, zinc and steel cannot read as neutral and the smoked speakers lose their tint.
changes.expected: Practicals stay warm but the shell greys out toward warm neutral; blue channel on the ceiling rises.

changes.problem: The haze makes hard diagonal shafts that read as a stage or nightclub, not a quiet listening bar.

evidence.measured: a visible bright diagonal beam from a ceiling spot across the back of the room

changes.expected: A faint softening around the lamps with no distinct beams; deeper back-of-room contrast.

changes.problem: The foreground chair back is a crushed black slab in the lower left and the frame shows almost no concrete or steel shell, which makes the room generic.

change.to: position [3.05, 2.0, 1.30], target [7.6, 5.2, 1.40], 35 mm, so the chair back drops out or clips only the corner and the right-hand wall's concrete enters the right edge

changes.expected: The counter leads cleanly to the niches; some board-formed concrete shows on the right; no dead black mass.

changes.problem: The Dome liners glow milky white, hiding their smoked tint and nearly clipping.
changes.expected: The Domes read as smoked acrylic with a soft inner glow; the light pools stay on the zinc from the downlights.

changes.problem: Timber and ceiling are smooth and uniform at 1:1; no checks, nail holes, grain variation or end grain.

evidence.measured: lum_range only 39.3 across the beams and ceiling; visually flat

change.setting: materials' finish: the fir beams and oak
change.to: fir with higher grain contrast, roughness variation 0.45 to 0.7, darker end grain and occasional checks; oak stain slightly darker with visible ray fleck

changes.expected: Beams and shelves gain texture and tonal variety; the ceiling's range widens.

out_of_scope.request: Vary the counter stools and chairs (different models or worn finishes) so they are not identical copies
out_of_scope.why: The seats are fixed by the card as part of the room's design

out_of_scope.request: Show more board-formed concrete and blackened steel in the shell rather than timber-lined niches and shelving
out_of_scope.why: The room's materials and the back bar are fixed; only the camera (c6) can bring more of the shell into frame

out_of_scope.request: Make the speakers' smoked acrylic darker or less transparent so the white batts do not dominate
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour and parts are EARF's products and fixed
